name: 02-preferential-attachment
title: Barabási–Albert preferential attachment
question: Does degree-proportional attachment produce scale-free hubs?
hypothesis: Linking new nodes preferentially to high-degree nodes yields a power-law degree distribution with a few dominant hubs.
objective: Run the preferential_attachment reaction and show how it reconfigures the network, measuring its signature structural observables.
description:
Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `preferential_attachment` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
claim: Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.

config.title: Barabási–Albert preferential attachment
config.subtitle: new nodes attach to existing nodes ∝ degree ('rich get richer')

expected_behavior.name: ba-forms-hubs
expected_behavior.condition: a few nodes accumulate far more edges than the mean
expected_behavior.rationale: 'Rich get richer' concentrates edges on early, high-degree nodes.

expected_behavior.name: ba-heavy-tail
expected_behavior.condition: the degree distribution is heavy-tailed (finite, non-Poisson), approaching the scale-free regime
expected_behavior.rationale: The BA model has an asymptotic exponent γ=3; at N≈60 the finite-size MLE is biased low, but the tail is clearly heavier than Erdős–Rényi.

behavior_tests.name: ba-hub-emerges
behavior_tests.description: The maximum degree reaches ≥10 (a dominant hub).

behavior_tests.name: ba-connected
behavior_tests.description: The network stays fully connected (BA growth never disconnects).

findings.name: preferential_attachment-signature
findings.summary: Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.
findings.detail: A clear hub emerges and the degree distribution is heavy-tailed, in contrast to the Erdős–Rényi baseline — the signature of preferential attachment. At N≈60 the maximum-likelihood exponent (γ≈1.5) is biased below the asymptotic BA value of 3, a known finite-size effect; the robust, scale-independent signal is that the maximum degree is several times the mean (vs the narrow Erdős–Rényi spread).

followup_proposals.title: Nonlinear preferential attachment & aging kernels
followup_proposals.motivation: This study used the linear BA kernel Π∝k; nonlinear (Π∝k^α) and node-aging kernels change whether a single hub dominates.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Add an attachment exponent α and an age-decay factor to the preferential_attachment reaction; sweep α to cross the super/sub-linear sync transition.
